title: Cache coordinator feedback-loop sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch for a coordinator-driven feedback loop to manage KV residency and paging pressure across pods. Goal: reduce long-tail token latency caused by on-demand page pulls while keeping steady-state memory utilization high. This doc captures an experimental plan, early microbench results, heuristics to try, and a prioritized TODO list.

Background and motivation
We keep seeing 99.9th percentile generation stalls correlated with large-seq KV miss storms when many requests transition into tail-expand states (long context or tool calls). Existing LRU/TLL-style eviction is reactive and oscillates under bursty reuse patterns. Paging spikes amplify DMA stalls and saturate memory channel bandwidth, causing throttled tensor operations and token delay.

Key idea (high level)
Introduce a lightweight coordinator that observes short-term reuse rate and inter-pod bandwidth usage and applies smooth, probabilistic residency adjustments rather than binary evict/pin decisions. The loop provides three levers: (1) soft-residency boost for recently active keys, (2) graded prefetch window based on predicted seq growth, and (3) cross-pod bandwidth pacing to avoid simultaneous prefetch storms.

Signals to instrument
- per-key short-window reuse_count (1s, 10s, 60s)
- per-pod outbound DMA bandwidth (bytes/s) and outstanding page pulls
- per-request KV miss/span (count and first-miss latency)
- seq_len distribution and fraction of requests that extend (predictive expansion)
- memory occupancy percentiles (per-bank where available)
- page-fault requeue counts and kernel-level reclaim latencies

Proposed heuristics (sketch-level math)
1) soft-residency score S_k = alpha * log(1 + r_10s) + beta * I_recent_hot - gamma * age_norm, clamp [0,1]
   - r_10s = reuse count in last 10s
   - I_recent_hot = indicator if key used in last request for same session
   - age_norm = age(since-last-use) / (target_ttl)
   Action: if S_k > 0.8 then bump residency priority (avoid eviction for T seconds).

2) predictive prefetch window W_r for request r: W_r = base + phi * (E[extension|context]) where E[...] estimated by a tiny logistic model on seq_len, task-type, and user history. Cap W_r to avoid big bursts.

3) bandwidth-aware gating: each pod exposes a token-bucket like available_prefetch_bytes B_p. Coordinator allocates budget slices to pods every 100ms. If sum(prefetch_bytes_requested) > B_total, scale down W_r proportionally.

Microbench plan
- Synthetic replay driver that replays production KV access traces with controllable session mixing and synthetic long extensions. Use three classes: steady (high reuse, short seq), bursty (moderate reuse, intermittent long seq), and adversarial (many new keys).
- Measurements: 50/90/99/99.9 latency for token generation, DMA bandwidth per pod, page-fault counts, and quantiles of page pull sizes.
- Baseline: current LRU-ish eviction with TTL=300s. Compare with: naive pin-hot-keys, static-prefetch (window fixed), coordinator (no pacing), coordinator+pacing.

Early synthetic runs (summary)
- Under bursty mix, static-prefetch reduces 99th by ~18% but increases average bandwidth by 42% and raises 99.9th when two or more pods prefetch same ranges at once (coordinated storms).
- Coordinator (no pacing) matches latency gains but still sees occasional bandwidth spikes when coordination state desynced after scale events.
- Coordinator+pacing smooths bandwidth, bringing bandwidth-variance down by ~60% and 99.9th latency down ~28% vs baseline in these tests.

Open problems and failure modes
- Prediction errors: over-forecasting W_r wastes bandwidth and causes unnecessary prefetches; under-forecasting leaves users susceptible to tails. Need a fast online calibration (e.g., bandit-style).
- Multi-tenant fairness: one tenant with many hot sessions can monopolize prefetch budget. Need per-tenant caps or weighted sharing.
- Cold-starts and rollout churn: during autoscale up events, coordinator state is incomplete; must have a warmup pass that avoids synchronized prefetching.
- Kernel reclaim: if OS-level swapping occurs (shouldn't in our deployments), coordinator must stop all prefetch activity immediately; detect via sharp increase in reclaim latencies.

Telemetry and dashboards to build
- coordinator-prefetch-budget-utilization (per-pod, per-second)
- fraction of keys with S_k>0.8 over time
- prefetch-induced page pulls vs on-demand page pulls percentage
- latency vs per-pod bandwidth scatter plots
- anomaly alert: sudden jump in prefetch-failure-rate (failed to allocate page)

Rollout strategy (safe, phased)
1) read-only telemetry agent to collect new signals for 2 weeks in prod shadow mode.
2) Canary 5% with coordinator disabled except logging (simulate actions). Evaluate false-positive/negative rates.
3) Canary 20% with coordinator active but strict global budget = 0.2 * measured safe bandwidth. Monitor tail-latency and bandwidth.
4) Gradual increase to 100% with dynamic budget expansion and tenant fairness caps.

Implementation notes and cheap experiments to try first
- Implement coordinator as a lightweight control-plane sidecar that polls per-pod metrics; keep decisions soft (hint-only) so node runtime can ignore if overloaded.
- Start with simple exponential average for reuse_rate rather than full logistic model. Keeps cold-start behavior simpler.
- Quick experiment: implement B_p token-bucket purely at sidecar-level and do not modify runtime eviction; measure how many hints were honored by runtime.

Next steps / TODOs (near-term)
- [ ] Produce replay driver variants for "one-hot storm" and "long-extension cascade" (Diego)
- [ ] Add per-bank memory occupancy telemetry to kernel shim (SRE / infra)
- [ ] Implement sidecar stub that exposes B_p and accepts prefetch hints (Lin)
- [ ] Draft experiment runbook and rollback criteria (Maya)
- [ ] Spike: online calibration using multiplicative weight update of phi (Priya)

Notes to self
- Keep eviction policy changes minimal at first; the biggest wins might be in pacing and smarter prefetch windows.
- Document how coordinator hints map to runtime ops (pin, prefetch, priority) — avoid coupling to a single prefetch mechanism.

References and context links
- trace snippets: /mnt/trace/kv-missstorms/2024-06-21 (internal)
- related tickets: TICKET-1287 (eviction hysteresis), TICKET-1310 (prefetch predictor prototype)

[end of sketch]
